Class NineAxisMotionShield

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.imu.NineAxisMotionShield
All Implemented Interfaces:
Accelerometer, Gyroscope, SampleProvider
public final class NineAxisMotionShield extends Object implements Accelerometer, Gyroscope, SampleProvider
The Bosch BNO055 orientation sensor of the Arduino 9 Axis Motion Shield, read over I2C as plain Java on top of I2c (so it needs no Arduino library). The sensor fuses its accelerometer and gyroscope itself, in the IMU fusion mode: the heading is relative to the direction the sensor pointed at construction, needs no compass calibration and is not disturbed by magnetic fields. 
NineAxisMotionShield imu = new NineAxisMotionShield();   // once, at startup
imu.reset();                                             // count the turn from here
// ... turn left until imu.getAngle() >= 270 (heading grows clockwise)

The shield's BNO055 answers at address 0x28. The board's reset line for the sensor is D7, so a program using the shield must not use D7 for anything else. new NineAxisMotionShield(gpio, i2c) drives that line and talks to the sensor through a given Gpio and I2c instead of the board's, which is how a unit test mocks them.
